newsitem.title: FRANCE: France aims to sell Lyonnais in two years.
newsitem.headline: France aims to sell Lyonnais in two years.

text.p: France plans to get Credit Lyonnais into shape to sell the state-owned bank in two years, a finance ministry spokeswoman said Friday.

The spokeswoman also said the finance ministry would hold off submitting a rescue plan for the bank to the European Union's executive body until the end of March as it looked for ways to limit the drain on public funds.
The rescue plan, which would be the third in four years for the bank, had been expected to be lodged in Brussels this week. It would require approval by the European Commission.
The spokeswoman said the decision to delay presentation of the plan had been made in cooperation with European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert.

"Both want to limit the amount of public money" needed for the bank, she said, adding that Van Miert wanted to ensure the the package respected EU competition rules and that French officials want to "respect the interests of French taxpapers."
She added that the aim of the plan would be to have the bank, whose woes stem from an expansion spree in the late 1980s, "in a state ready to privatise in two years from now."
Credit Lyonnais, which once set out to fulfil a government dream of putting French banking on the world map, received a 45 billion franc ($7.9 billion) bailout just two years ago.
